result.summary: The street environment is characterized by a significant lack of pedestrian infrastructure, most notably the absence of a paved sidewalk on the left side of the roadway. While a narrow walkway exists on the right, the overall design prioritizes vehicle movement and parking over pedestrian safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalk
hazards.description: The left side of the street lacks a paved walkway, forcing pedestrians to walk on unpaved dirt or in the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground and midground adjacent to the brick building

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Parked cars along the right curb limit sightlines between drivers and pedestrians attempting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway

hazards.name: Poor Pavement Condition
hazards.description: The unpaved area on the left is uneven and likely to be hazardous in wet conditions.
hazards.location_in_image: Left foreground

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct a continuous, ADA-compliant paved sidewalk on the left side of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install marked crosswalks at the nearest intersections to provide safe, designated crossing points.

interventions.title: Street Lighting
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lighting to improve visibility and safety during nighttime hours.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a narrow, poorly maintained sidewalk that is significantly obstructed by utility poles. The presence of a vacant lot and the lack of a physical buffer from the roadway further reduces the safety and comfort for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Utility poles in walkway
hazards.description: Two large utility poles are positioned directly in the narrow sidewalk path, forcing pedestrians to step into the street or onto unpaved ground.
hazards.location_in_image: Center-left, directly on the paved walkway behind the parked car

hazards.name: Poor sidewalk condition
hazards.description: The sidewalk surface is narrow, cracked, and uneven, creating significant trip hazards and accessibility barriers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the left side of the image, running parallel to the street

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian-scale lighting
hazards.description: No dedicated street lighting is visible, which may create safety concerns for pedestrians during nighttime hours.
hazards.location_in_image: Throughout the visible streetscape

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening and Reconstruction
interventions.description: Reconstruct the sidewalk to provide a minimum of 5-6 feet of clear, level walking space to meet accessibility standards.

interventions.title: Utility Pole Relocation
interventions.description: Relocate utility poles to a furniture zone or underground the lines to remove physical obstructions from the pedestrian clear zone.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Lighting Installation
interventions.description: Install pedestrian-scale street lights to improve visibility and personal security along the walkway.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a residential street characterized by narrow sidewalks and a lack of dedicated crossing infrastructure. High levels of on-street parking further restrict visibility and narrow the effective roadway, creating potential conflicts between pedestrians and vehicles.

hazards.name: Narrow Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk on the left side of the street is significantly narrower than standard accessibility requirements, making it difficult for pedestrians to pass each other.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the street, adjacent to the brick building

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures the view of pedestrians for oncoming traffic, especially at potential crossing points.
hazards.location_in_image: Both sides of the street where cars are parked parallel to the curb

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at intersections to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Widening
interventions.description: Expand the existing narrow sidewalks to provide a safer and more accessible walking environment for all users.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crossings at intersections to designate safe pedestrian paths and alert drivers to their presence.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a narrow, poorly maintained sidewalk that is partially overgrown with vegetation and obstructed by debris. There are no marked crossings or pedestrian-specific safety infrastructure, forcing pedestrians to navigate a degraded path adjacent to parked vehicles.

hazards.name: Degraded Sidewalk
hazards.description: The sidewalk is narrow, cracked, and overgrown with grass, making it difficult to traverse.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the image along the building frontage.

hazards.name: Debris and Obstructions
hazards.description: Wooden framing and loose debris are present near the walkway, creating potential trip hazards.
hazards.location_in_image: Near the base of the brick building on the left.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Reconstruction
interventions.description: Repair and widen the sidewalk to meet ADA standards and provide a clear, level walking surface.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Install street lighting to improve visibility and safety for pedestrians at night.
